misconceptions.description: Treating development as software programming only
misconceptions.trigger: learner excludes writing, storyboarding, media production, or assessment authoring from development work
misconceptions.feedback: Development includes any activity that turns the design blueprint into usable instructional assets, including text, media, interactions, assessment items, and prototypes.

misconceptions.description: Reducing implementation to uploading the course
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores facilitator preparation, delivery logistics, or LMS setup
misconceptions.feedback: Implementation is broader than publishing. It includes rollout conditions, facilitator readiness, communication, access, and platform reliability.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a prototype should already behave like the final polished course
misconceptions.trigger: learner rejects rough prototypes because they are incomplete
misconceptions.feedback: A prototype is valuable because it is unfinished. It helps teams surface design issues early before full production cost is committed.
